semantic_insights: DOI 10.13026/8xbn-nq66 uses the PhysioNet prefix 10.13026, which matches the stated publisher https://physionet.org and the page URL, so identifier, publisher and landing page are mutually corroborating.

Grant identifiers follow valid NIH patterns: OT2OD032720 decomposes as activity code OT2, institute OD, serial 032720; 3OT2OD032720-01S1 and 3OT2OD032720-01S3 are well-formed type-3 supplement numbers with support year 01; 1OT2OD032720-01 is a well-formed new-award number. The grantor named (NIH Common Fund, Bridge2AI program) is consistent with the OT2 Other Transaction mechanism and with purposes that describe a Bridge2AI data generation project.

The tiered access design is coherent end to end: sensitive_elements identifies raw voice as biometric and identifying; is_deidentified excludes raw waveforms from the release; participant_privacy describes controlled access for audio; data_governance.access_review_process specifies registered access for features versus DACO review plus institutional sign-off for audio; related_datasets records the Synapse raw-audio target with a derives_from relationship; and informed_consent.consent_scope covers exactly these two release tiers. Five independent fields tell the same story.

HIPAA Safe Harbor supplemented by indirect-identifier removal, geographic generalization to country, removal of narrative text and free-speech transcripts, and withholding of spectrogram-family features derived from open-response prompts is a method appropriate to health data whose primary modality is inherently identifying.

Element 8 sub-element 4 is satisfied by software in a transforming role, not merely a capture or hosting role: b2aiprep version 3.0.0 is named as the library that assembled the released phenotype tables and derived features, with torchaudio, openSMILE, Praat via Parselmouth, Speech Articulatory Coding and ppgs named as the producers of specific distributed feature files. The tablet capture application and PhysioNet hosting are documented too but are not what earns the point.

Preprocessing parameters are given at a level that supports replication: 16 kHz monaural resampling with a Butterworth anti-aliasing filter, 25 ms window, 10 ms hop, 400-point FFT, 60 Mel bins, sparc at 50 Hz, torchaudio pitch over 80-500 Hz and sparc pitch over 50-550 Hz, phonetic posteriorgrams over 40 phoneme categories at 100 Hz.

Temporal ordering is internally consistent: grant period September 2022 to November 2026 encloses a 12-month collection window, releases run November 2024, January 2025, April 2025, August 2025, December 2025 and May 2026, and the issued date 2026-05-01 matches the v3.1.0 release date.

known_biases uses five distinct BiasTypeEnum-aligned categories (selection, sampling, representation, measurement, annotation) rather than a single undifferentiated bias statement, and three carry mitigation strategies while two carry affected_subsets.

The record uses source_caveats as a first-class device at nine points, recording where the PhysioNet release, the project documentation, the IRB protocol and the feasibility publication disagree and which source was preferred. This is unusual and materially raises the trustworthiness of the contested values (recording totals, hosting institution, enrollment target, award numbers).

Absence of imputation is documented positively rather than left silent: missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy states no imputation was performed and that a missingness table is generated by the audit protocol and shipped with the dataset.

The self-assessment recorded in notes discloses where the consortium's own AI-readiness scoring falls short (data quality not met, contextualized not met, sustainability at 50 percent), which is corroborated by the methodological_limitation entry rather than contradicted by it.

The w3id.org URI is a persistent-identifier service appropriate for schema identification. The B2AI CURIEs are well formed prefix:number identifiers consistent with the Bridge2AI program affiliation asserted in funders and description.

The nearest content is file_collections[phenotype].description, which enumerates table names ('confounders.tsv', 'demographics.tsv', the 18 diagnosis tables, the 13 questionnaire instruments, the 7 task tables) and states each table is 'paired with a JSON data dictionary keyed by column name'; instances[1].label_description names participant_id, session_id and task name as the recording identifiers; participant_privacy.data_linkage names participant_id and session_id as the join keys
sub_elements.quality_note: The record establishes that variable-level documentation exists and where it lives, and it names the three linking variables, but supplies no variable metadata itself: no identifiers, types, units, permissible values or descriptions for any of the phenotype columns or feature fields. elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition satisfied on E1 and E8 evidence: description states '833 adult participants collected at five sites' recruited 'at high-volume expert clinics'; collection_mechanisms describes a supervised protocol administered to participants. The governance condition is independently satisfied on E2 evidence (confidentiality_level 'restricted', Certificate of Confidentiality), but is not needed here.
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: two entries - University of South Florida IRB (single IRB with subsite IRBs approved through the sIRB process; approval covers both the clinical study and the data collection and sharing; not a drug or device study; no data monitoring committee) and the Canadian research ethics boards (Mount Sinai Hospital, The Hospital for Sick Children, University of Toronto, applying separately because Canadian institutions fall outside the US sIRB process, with copies submitted to the USF IRB; genomic work under a separate protocol). human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects: true with irb_approval, ethics_review_board and regulatory_compliance (partial HIPAA waiver for chart review during screening; Certificate of Confidentiality). data_protection_impacts: ethicist team review identifying sensitive fields for removal, plus a published memorandum justifying controlled access for raw voice on re-identification and misuse grounds. data_governance.committee_name: DACO with contact address.
sub_elements.quality_note: Oversight is documented at the level of who approved what, under which regulatory mechanism, and how a cross-border complication was handled - the Canadian sIRB exception is the kind of detail that is normally omitted. The DPIA component is present in substance: a named review activity, a stated finding (which fields to remove) and a published justification for the access restriction that followed.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Consistency check passes: involves_human_subjects is true and IRB approval is populated as required. The record itself flags in data_protection_impacts.source_caveats that the healthsheet answered 'No' to whether a formal impact analysis was conducted; that tension is recorded as a low-severity issue rather than treated as a failure, because the activities described do constitute an impact assessment in substance and the discrepancy is disclosed rather than hidden. sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods: four entries with typed booleans and details - was_directly_observed (acoustic data recorded during a supervised session on the tablet application with a head-mounted headset microphone where possible); was_reported_by_subjects (demographics, confounders such as smoking and hydration status, and validated questionnaires self-reported through the application); was_validated_verified (clinical diagnoses verified by clinicians reviewing audio and imaging, consulting EHRs or checking prescriptions against per-cohort gold standards); was_inferred_derived (all released features derived computationally from standardized audio using the b2aiprep pipeline). raw_data_sources supplies three matching source entries with formats and access details.
sub_elements.quality_note: Each acquisition modality is flagged and described, so a reuser can tell for any given variable whether it was observed, self-reported, clinically verified or computed - which is the distinction that determines how a variable should be treated in analysis.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The four modalities partition the dataset's content without overlap or gap, and each maps onto a documented component: observed to audio, self-reported to the phenotype questionnaire tables, verified to the diagnosis tables, derived to the feature Parquet files. The derived flag correctly identifies that everything in the registered-access release is computed rather than observed, which is consistent with is_deidentified withholding waveforms.

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Software-output condition satisfied on E10/E8 external_resources evidence: the record references code repositories at https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep and https://github.com/sensein/senselab, and the REDCap instrument repository archived at Zenodo.
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: six entries - conversion to monaural and resampling to 16 kHz with a Butterworth anti-aliasing filter; STFT with 25 ms window, 10 ms hop, 400-point FFT, spectrograms downsampled by two in time, Mel spectrograms with 60 Mel bins and 60 MFCCs derived from them; sparc articulatory features at 50 Hz giving six vocal tract articulator traces plus loudness, periodicity and pitch, with torchaudio pitch over 80-500 Hz and sparc pitch over 50-550 Hz; openSMILE acoustic features and Parselmouth/Praat phonetic and prosodic features; de-identification removing Safe Harbor identifiers, state and province, narrative text and free-speech transcripts and withholding spectrogram-family features from free speech; conversion to BIDS v1.9.0 and assembly with b2aiprep version 3.0.0. cleaning_strategies: two entries, recording that no cleaning pre-processing was applied and describing the audit protocol instead (missingness tables, distribution and outlier checks, categorical validation against the schema, audio QC metrics including silence proportion, waveform duration and comparison of produced speech against the intended passage). labeling_strategies: clinical assessment per cohort with annotations_per_item: 1, annotator_demographics, data_annotation_platform (REDCap plus the tablet application), data_annotation_protocol (gold standard label, clinician-diagnosed, Bridge2AI protocols and ICD-10) and inter_annotator_agreement. machine_annotation_tools: nine tools with tool_descriptions and tool_accuracy.
sub_elements.quality_note: Preprocessing is given at parameter level - window, hop, FFT size, Mel bin count, sample rate, pitch ranges - which is the threshold for actual replicability rather than narrative description. Annotation quality is addressed directly and unflatteringly: one labeler per instance, no adjudication, no inter-annotator agreement computable, and off-the-shelf derivation models unaudited for correctness.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Parameters are internally consistent and technically coherent: a 25 ms window at 16 kHz corresponds to 400 samples, matching the stated 400-point FFT exactly; MFCCs derived from 60 Mel bins is a standard chain. The v1.1-versus-v3.1.0 parameter change (512-point FFT, no time downsampling) is disclosed in source_caveats rather than conflated. cleaning_strategies' claim that no cleaning was applied is consistent with missing_data_documentation stating no imputation was performed - the record is coherent in treating quality as audited-and-reported rather than corrected. imputation_protocols is not populated as a slot, but the absence of imputation is affirmatively documented.

sub_elements.name: Software and Tools Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Element 8's datasets-shared condition is satisfied and the released data was demonstrably processed (preprocessing_strategies and acquisition_methods.was_inferred_derived establish that every distributed file is a computed derivation). Per #1081 this sub-element is not gated on whether a repository is pointed at; it is scored for any dataset that was processed at all.
sub_elements.evidence: machine_annotation_tools.tools names openSMILE, Praat, Parselmouth, torchaudio, Speech Articulatory Coding (sparc), ppgs, b2aiprep, senselab and OpenAI Whisper Large, with tool_descriptions stating what each produced. preprocessing_strategies names b2aiprep 'version 3.0.0 for this release' as the library that assembled the phenotype tables and derived features, and attributes specific outputs to specific tools (torchaudio for pitch, spectrograms, Mel spectrograms and MFCCs; sparc for articulography, loudness, periodicity and pitch; ppgs for phonetic posteriorgrams; openSMILE for eGeMAPS acoustic features; Praat via Parselmouth for fundamental frequency, formants and voice quality). external_resources gives repositories https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep (Apache-2.0) and https://github.com/sensein/senselab.
sub_elements.quality_note: The evidence is carried by machine_annotation_tools, preprocessing_strategies prose and external_resources, any one of which would satisfy the requirement that the field exist. A reader can tell exactly which software produced each distributed feature file, and for the principal pipeline can obtain the source and pin the version.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Threshold met on transforming-role software, not on capture or hosting. b2aiprep 3.0.0 produced the released feature and phenotype files; torchaudio, sparc, ppgs, openSMILE and Praat/Parselmouth each produced named files in the distribution. These fall squarely inside the processing role rather than any of the excluded roles. The tablet acquisition application (role a, capture) and PhysioNet (role b, hosting) are also documented but are not what earns the point, and their presence neither adds nor subtracts. Whisper Large sits closest to role (e) since the transcripts it produced were removed from the release, so it is not relied on. A version is given for the principal pipeline and repositories are resolvable, which exceeds the naming threshold the sub-element sets.

sub_elements.name: External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition satisfied as above.
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: seven entries with URLs, licenses and archival flags - b2aiprep (Apache-2.0), senselab, the REDCap data dictionary and instrument PDFs (MIT, archived at Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.12760724), the documentation site and its source (MIT, archived at Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.13834653), consortium FHIR profiles for voice as a biomarker, the Interspeech 2024 protocol publication with its ISCA archive URL, and the Bridge2AI Voice Scholars training program. conforms_to: BIDS v1.9.0. The imputation question is answered affirmatively in the negative, with the alternative (a shipped missingness table) named, which the sub-element explicitly accepts.

The record's honesty about persistence is preserved - one entry's future_guarantees records that the healthsheet answered 'NA' on persistence guarantees and official archival versions. elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Known Limitations Documented
sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations: six typed entries - coverage_limitation (English only; Spanish protocol under development and not in this release); representativeness_limitation (sample of a larger ongoing collection at five North American sites); temporal_limitation (changes in diagnostic criteria or clinical practice over the collection period as a source of distribution shift); scope_limitation (raw waveforms absent; spectrogram-family features withheld for sensitive records, audio checks and free speech, so analyses needing the original signal or open-response acoustic detail are impossible on the registered-access files); integration_limitation (laryngoscopy, brain imaging, respiratory function tests, genomic data and other EHR content extracted at sites and not included); methodological_limitation (internal audit for missingness and consistency, but the AI-readiness self-assessment records data quality as not met and human-level performance on the supported tasks varies widely).
sub_elements.quality_note: Six limitations across distinct axes, each typed and each stating the concrete analytical consequence rather than a generic caveat. The scope limitation tells a user precisely which analyses this release cannot support, and the methodological entry surfaces the consortium's own negative self-assessment.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Each limitation is corroborated elsewhere: the English-only constraint matches the neurological cohort eligibility in subsets and the representation_bias entry; the scope limitation matches is_deidentified and the v2.0 erratum; the integration limitation matches raw_data_sources[2].access_details. The methodological entry agrees with notes, which records data quality as not met in the AI-readiness self-assessment - the datasheet does not contradict its own scorecard.

sub_elements.name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
sub_elements.evidence: known_biases: five entries using distinct bias_type values - selection_bias (recruitment from high-volume expert clinics at a limited number of academic institutions, reflecting specialty referral patterns rather than the general population; affected_subsets given); sampling_bias (non-probability sample from an ongoing collection at limited geographic locations; mitigation_strategy of shifting to remote collection and controlling for more variables); representation_bias (English fluency requirement; skews by disorder, site and demographics; groups with less trust in the medical system or in AI, or living further from sites, less likely to be recruited; mitigation_strategy advising users to consider the multivariate distribution); measurement_bias (screening for different disorders by site, confounding cohort membership with site and with the particular tablet device; affected_subsets given); annotation_bias (a single labeler per instance, so labels carry that clinician's judgment without adjudication). future_use_impacts records skew-driven risks of unfair treatment and quality-of-service harms.
sub_elements.quality_note: Five distinct taxonomy categories rather than one undifferentiated statement, with three carrying mitigation strategies and two carrying affected_subsets. The representation_bias entry identifies a recruitment mechanism - differential trust in the medical system and in AI - that most datasheets omit entirely.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The bias_type values map onto the BiasTypeEnum categories and each is used correctly for the phenomenon described: measurement_bias is correctly applied to device and site confounding rather than being conflated with selection; annotation_bias correctly describes single-labeler judgment. The social-impact dimension required by the sub-element's RAI scope is carried by future_use_impacts, which names the harm classes (unfair treatment of groups, quality of service) rather than gesturing at risk. The biases are consistent with sampling_strategies (is_random false, is_representative false) and with subpopulations.distribution.

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies: six entries - differing collection configurations across sites and protocol change over the study; noise artifacts and varying recording distance from the head-mounted headset microphone; diagnostic practice varying between clinicians and sites, with diagnosis sometimes from a single clinician, an EHR or an active prescription; possible questionnaire inaccuracy and participant underreporting; derived text such as transcription produced by unaudited off-the-shelf models; some audio files unable to generate certain derived features because of length or other issues, and therefore absent from the corresponding feature files.
sub_elements.quality_note: The anomalies span acquisition, labeling, self-report and derivation, and the last one explains an observable property of the distributed files - the differing per-feature record counts - so a user encountering that discrepancy finds it already accounted for.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The final anomaly is directly corroborated by instances[1].notes, where the per-feature counts differ (32,522 down to 28,640) for exactly the stated reasons, and by missing_data_documentation.missing_data_patterns. The transcription anomaly matches machine_annotation_tools.tool_accuracy verbatim in substance. The site-configuration anomaly matches collection_mechanisms' statement that distinct devices were used at each site. No anomaly is asserted without a corroborating mechanism elsewhere in the record.

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements: four entries each with sensitive_elements_present: true and sensitivity_details - race and ethnicity from the demographics instrument; sexual orientation; socioeconomic and health information including diagnosis, psychiatric history and validated questionnaire responses covering depression, anxiety, PTSD and ADHD symptoms; raw voice recordings as biometric data capable of identifying the speaker, excluded from the registered-access release. content_warnings: content_warnings_present: true with a warning that free speech tasks were recorded in open-response form and that offensive or distressing content, while unlikely, cannot be completely avoided since participants choose their own language, plus a source_caveat reconciling the healthsheet's framing with the v3.0.0 and v3.1.0 removal of free-speech transcripts and spectrogram-family features. confidential_elements: confidential_elements_present: false with the basis stated.
sub_elements.quality_note: Sensitivity is itemized by category rather than asserted in aggregate, and the content warning is qualified with the residual exposure actually remaining in the released files after the transcript removals - which is the practically useful statement.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The sensitive categories align exactly with the removals listed in is_deidentified.identifiers_removed (household income, mental health status, traumatic life experiences, biometric identifiers), so the record identifies a risk and shows the corresponding control. The confidential_elements: false finding concerns legal privilege and non-public communications, a distinct concept from sensitivity, so it does not contradict the four sensitive_elements entries. Treating raw voice as biometric and therefore identifying is technically correct.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: two entries - the USF single IRB with subsite IRBs through the sIRB process, covering both the clinical study and the data collection and sharing, with the not-a-drug-or-device and no-DMC findings; and the Canadian research ethics boards at Mount Sinai Hospital, The Hospital for Sick Children and the University of Toronto, which applied separately because Canadian institutions fall outside the US sIRB process, with approved applications submitted to the USF IRB and a separate University of Toronto and Mount Sinai protocol covering genomic work. future_use_impacts: two entries - skews by disorder, site and demographics, with the warning that models trained without accounting for them risk unfair treatment of groups, quality-of-service problems or other harms; and the anticipated benefit that voice-based assessment integrated into digital health tools could advance early detection, continuous monitoring and personalized treatment, and extend screening to low-resource settings. data_protection_impacts adds the ethicist review and the published memorandum on controlled access, naming re-identification by voice, voice hacking and data ownership as challenges requiring a governance framework.
sub_elements.quality_note: Both halves of the sub-element are substantive: the ethical review is documented at the level of which body reviewed what under which regulatory framework, and the social impact analysis names both downside harm classes and upside benefits rather than only one direction.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The downside impacts follow logically from the biases documented in known_biases, so the impact analysis is derived from the dataset's actual properties rather than generic. Conflicts of interest are not separately declared, a minor gap against the sub-element's full scope, but ethical review and social impact - its two named components - are both well covered. The governance-framework concerns named in data_protection_impacts (voice hacking, data ownership) are specific to the voice modality rather than boilerplate.

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition satisfied: distribution_formats with access_urls, versioned PhysioNet landing page, license permitting research reuse.
sub_elements.evidence: publisher: https://physionet.org; page: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; status: published; maintainers records that the dataset is hosted on PhysioNet, maintained by the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology, 'which provides the technical infrastructure and continued access for credentialed researchers'; distribution_formats access_urls resolve to PhysioNet; the controlled-access tier is published through Synapse (syn72370534).
sub_elements.quality_note: PhysioNet is a recognized domain repository for clinical physiological data, and the record identifies not only the platform but the institution maintaining it and the access model it provides. A second recognized platform (Synapse) carries the controlled-access tier.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The publisher is corroborated by the DOI prefix 10.13026, which is PhysioNet's, and by the page URL - identifier, publisher and landing page agree. The hosting conflict with the project documentation's Health Data Nexus claim is disclosed and resolved in maintainers.source_caveats, which attributes the Health Data Nexus description to the earlier v1.0 release; that resolution is independently corroborated by related_datasets, where v1.0 carries the Health Data Nexus DOI prefix 10.57764 while all later versions carry 10.13026.

sub_elements.name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition satisfied as above; per #1080 this sub-element is scored on the shared condition alone and does not require a prior publication to become applicable.
sub_elements.evidence: citation: full formatted citation naming twenty authors plus the final author, the title, '(version 3.1.0)', the publisher PhysioNet, 'RRID:SCR_007345' and 'https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66'. doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66. version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42 for version-independent citation. external_resources cites the Interspeech 2024 protocol publication with its ISCA archive URL.
sub_elements.quality_note: A ready-to-use citation string in a recognized format, carrying author list, version, publisher, repository RRID and a resolvable DOI URL, plus a concept DOI for citing the dataset independently of version. Both citation needs - this version and the dataset as such - are served.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The citation is internally consistent with title, version, publisher and doi, and its author order matches the creators list order. The RRID is well formed but scopes to PhysioNet as a resource rather than to this dataset, recorded as a low-severity correctness observation; dataset-level cross-referencing rests on the DOI, which is valid and prefix-plausible. The version-independent DOI is correctly distinguished from the versioned one.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition satisfied as above.
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: 'Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) v1.9.0'; conforms_to_standard: [BIDS]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; file_collections[b2ai-voice-audio] declares BIDS conformance with a BIDS-compliant path template and dataset_description.json; external_resources records consortium-published FHIR profiles for voice as a biomarker; purposes states the intent to create bioinformatics standards for acoustic data; the Interspeech 2024 publication documents the multi-disorder protocol development.
sub_elements.quality_note: The dataset both conforms to community standards and contributes to them - BIDS organization for the audio, a public metadata schema for this record, FHIR profiles published back to the clinical interoperability community, and a protocol standardization paper.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Standards are named with versions where versions matter (BIDS v1.9.0) and the declared conformance is substantiated by the concrete artifacts listed - CHANGES.md, README.md, dataset_description.json and the sub-/ses-/task- path template are genuine BIDS requirements, so the claim is evidenced rather than asserted. ICD-10 is named in labeling_strategies as the diagnostic coding standard, adding a clinical terminology standard to the organizational and metadata ones.

sub_elements.name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition satisfied as above.
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources includes the project documentation site and dashboards at https://docs.b2ai-voice.org/ (source at https://github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-docs, archived at Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.13834653, MIT); training opportunities through the Bridge2AI Voice Scholars program at https://www.b2aivoicescholars.org/; the Interspeech 2024 protocol publication at its ISCA archive URL; the REDCap data dictionary, metadata and instrument PDFs at https://github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap archived at Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.12760724. page: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/. extension_mechanism.contribution_url: https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep, with discussion forums and issue pages for public discussion and pull requests accepted.
sub_elements.quality_note: A documentation site with dashboards, a named training program, a published protocol paper, downloadable survey instruments and an open contribution channel with forums and issue tracking. This covers the outreach dimension well beyond a single documentation link.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: URLs are structurally valid and their domains are consistent with the actors named elsewhere (eipm for the Weill Cornell institute named in creators, sensein for the b2aiprep maintainers). Archival status is stated per resource, so a user can distinguish the persistent copies from the live sites. The contribution mechanism in extension_mechanism corroborates the community-engagement claim with a concrete channel.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition satisfied as above.
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: six entries each with a relationship_type, a target_dataset identifier and a description - derives_from https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/ (the controlled-access raw audio the features were computed from); is_supplemented_by doi:10.13026/h995-bt35 (the Bridge2AI-Voice Pediatric Dataset, 23,533 recordings from 300 participants aged 2 to 18 at The Hospital for Sick Children); is_new_version_of doi:10.13026/k81f-qr68 (v3.0.0, 16 December 2025); is_new_version_of doi:10.13026/249v-w155 (v1.1, 17 January 2025); is_new_version_of doi:10.57764/qb6h-em84 (v1.0 on Health Data Nexus, which provided cloud compute rather than downloads); is_version_of doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42 (the version-independent DOI).
sub_elements.quality_note: Four distinct relationship types across six links, every one resolvable and every one accompanied by a description that explains what the target is and why it relates - including the substantive detail that the pediatric sibling covers ages 2 to 18 and that v1.0 operated on a compute-only model.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Relationship types are semantically correct in each case and the graph is internally consistent: the version chain matches version_access.versions_available and distribution_dates.release_dates; the derives_from target matches the Synapse accession in raw_data_sources and distribution_formats; the pediatric sibling is consistent with at_risk_populations.notes, which records that the pediatric cohort is published as a separate dataset, and with informed_consent's mention of parental permission and child assent for that arm. The platform change at v1.0 is reflected in a different DOI prefix, corroborating the migration.

strengths: Exceptional cross-field coherence: claims are corroborated across independent fields rather than asserted once. The tiered access design alone is told consistently by sensitive_elements, is_deidentified, participant_privacy, data_governance, related_datasets and informed_consent.consent_scope, and the v3.1.0 change list is independently confirmed by file_collections, cleaning_strategies and the errata.

Disciplined and unusual use of source_caveats at nine points to record where the PhysioNet release, the project documentation, the IRB protocol and the feasibility publication disagree, and which source was preferred - covering recording totals, hosting institution, enrollment target, award identifiers, FFT parameters and collection dates. Disagreement is surfaced rather than smoothed away.

Preprocessing documented at replication-grade parameter level (16 kHz monaural with Butterworth anti-aliasing, 25 ms window, 10 ms hop, 400-point FFT, 60 Mel bins, sparc at 50 Hz, pitch ranges of 80-500 Hz and 50-550 Hz), with each released feature family attributed to the specific software that produced it and the assembly pipeline pinned to b2aiprep version 3.0.0.

Ethics documentation complete across all five sub-elements, including the cross-border sIRB exception for the Canadian sites, a partial HIPAA waiver, a Certificate of Confidentiality with its legal effect stated, fully specified compensation with session and total caps, and a withdrawal mechanism that states frankly where withdrawal is no longer possible.

Candid negative disclosure throughout: k-anonymity with k greater than or equal to two is explicitly not achieved; a single labeler per instance with no adjudication and no computable inter-annotator agreement; off-the-shelf derivation models unaudited for correctness; the consortium's own AI-readiness self-assessment recording data quality as not met; v1.1 files withdrawn despite the stated support policy.

Provenance and version tracking are complete end to end - six releases with dates and DOIs, a concept DOI, three itemized errata, three raw data sources each with format and current access status, and a derives_from link to the resolvable Synapse accession for the withheld audio.
weaknesses: No variables field anywhere in the record. Variable-level metadata is documented only by reference - the reuser is told that JSON data dictionaries exist and are keyed by column name, and is given the three linking variables, but no column identifiers, types, units or permissible values appear in the datasheet. This is the single largest reuse gap and costs a point at Element 3 sub-element 4.

Only four keywords (voice, health, biomarkers, bridge2ai), covering domain and program affiliation but no condition, method, modality or standard. The record contains an exceptionally rich vocabulary for keywording - eighteen named conditions, six feature families, BIDS, ICD-10 - and surfaces none of it for discovery. Costs a point at Element 1 sub-element 3.

at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included is false while the cohorts include mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease, other dementias, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and substance use disorder. The prose reconciles this by recording that self-consent capacity was an eligibility requirement, but the boolean as it stands understates the cohort composition to any automated consumer.

Several canonical slots are unpopulated while their content is carried elsewhere: download_url (covered by distribution_formats.access_urls and page), is_tabular (unset despite substantially tabular content), was_derived_from (covered by raw_data_sources and the derives_from relationship), imputation_protocols (covered by the affirmative no-imputation statement) and data_governance.committee_contact (the DACO address sits in access_review_process). Each is a placement rather than a substance gap, but each weakens machine consumption.
Character encoding is not stated for the TSV and JSON components, the one gap in the format-standardization scope at Element 3 sub-element 2.

The stated semi-annual update cadence does not match the observed release dates, which run closer to quarterly through 2025. The record discloses the discrepancy itself, but leaves the two figures standing side by side rather than resolving which governs.
Conflicts of interest are not declared anywhere, a minor gap against the full scope of Element 9 sub-element 5, whose ethical-review and social-impact components are otherwise well covered.
recommendations: Add a variables block carrying at least the linking variables (participant_id, session_id) and the principal phenotype and feature columns with identifiers, types, units and permissible values, or attach a resolvable per-file data dictionary URL to each file_collections entry so the column semantics are reachable without obtaining the release.

Expand keywords from four to a set covering conditions (laryngeal cancer, Parkinson's disease, ALS, depression, chronic cough, airway stenosis), methods (acoustic biomarkers, audiomics, machine learning, MFCC, spectrogram, phonetic posteriorgram), modalities (speech, cough, respiratory sound) and standards (BIDS, ICD-10), all of which the record already contains.

Set at_risk_groups_included to true and describe the decisional-capacity assessment and consent safeguards applied to the cognitive impairment and psychiatric cohorts, rather than resolving the question with a false boolean qualified only in prose.

Populate the canonical slots whose content already exists elsewhere: download_url with the versioned PhysioNet files URL, is_tabular for the phenotype and static feature components, was_derived_from with the Synapse accession, imputation_protocols with the no-imputation determination and the missingness-table reference, and data_governance.committee_contact with DACO@b2ai-voice.org.
State the character encoding of the TSV and JSON components so format standardization is complete for Element 3 sub-element 2.
Reconcile the update cadence: state the observed release rhythm as operative and retain the documented semi-annual figure as the stated policy commitment, labelling which is which.

Qualify is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present with the standard under which it holds (no HIPAA Safe Harbor identifiers present) and place the residual quasi-identifier risk beside it, so the flag and the k-anonymity admission read as one coherent statement.
